<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `resolveObjectMasker (4 routes)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **39** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 465c2bea3ae57c41332908bae2e4e932a235f325` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f0f9611ef9fcae227f5873b3baca6d9805ac579a` — the merge of head `c97eb416db5710fcd97a0193aa5f2f7433248331` into base `465c2bea3ae57c41332908bae2e4e932a235f325`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f0f9611ef9fcae227f5873b3baca6d9805ac579a && git checkout f0f9611ef9fcae227f5873b3baca6d9805ac579a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 465c2bea3ae57c41332908bae2e4e932a235f325 c97eb416db5710fcd97a0193aa5f2f7433248331 && git checkout -B drift-repro 465c2bea3ae57c41332908bae2e4e932a235f325 && git merge --no-ff c97eb416db5710fcd97a0193aa5f2f7433248331

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 465c2bea3ae57c41332908bae2e4e932a235f325
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 465c2bea3ae57c41332908bae2e4e932a235f325` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c97eb416db5710fcd97a0193aa5f2f7433248331`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.test.ts, packages/rest/src/index.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-params-enforcement.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-object-schema-mask.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, .changeset/meta-action-entry-field-mask.md, content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx, content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx + docs/adr/0106-metadata-plane-fls-object-schema-masking.md, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-search-and-cache.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-collection-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-representation-validator.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, packages/client-react/src/metadata-hooks.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/setup/PackagedActionsSection.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/setup/packagedActions.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useNavActionDispatch.ts

Reviewed 2026-11-07T08:52Z on the face the changeset's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line decides: `record-recognisers --paths` over the file list names no face of its own and defers to that line, which carries the `(narrowing)` arm, so the narrowing face and this tier. Read: the PR body, the file list, the three-dot diff against the merge base on `main`, the head's check-runs, and the cited code on `main`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

Check-runs on this head at review time: every concluded run is success or skipped (PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Spec property liveness, Test UI, Flag docs affected). Nine are still in progress: Build Core, Build Docs, the four Type Check legs, the eight Test Core shards counted as their parent, the six Lint legs and Live E2E UI. The PASS below is conditional on those going green; a red among them returns the head to the dev, not to this record.

### ① Derived judgments

The one rule, as shipped. `projectMetaActionForCaller` (`@objectstack/rest`) builds the document `{ ...ownObject, actions: [entry] }` and hands it to `projectMetaObjectSchema` over `relateObjectSchemaMaskPosture`, so an entry is withheld exactly where `GET /meta/object/:name` already drops it from that object's `actions` on `main`: a param whose `field` the caller cannot read on the object the param names (`objectOverride` first, else the owner), or any other position of the entry that reads such a field (`maskDeniedFieldReferences`, `actionParamReadsDenied`). An entry that survives is served as declared, never rewritten. A `passthrough` posture (D4-exempt caller, no `security` service, mask switched off) serves every entry with no object read, so those callers are byte-identical to `main` by construction. An owner-less entry, or one whose owner names no object definition, is judged through the two new `@objectstack/metadata-core` helpers, which call the same `maskDeniedFieldReferences` with an empty own-denied set and the caller's readable set per named object; a named object whose posture cannot be evaluated, or is undetermined, is related as `undefined`, which the existing `MaskScope.related` rule already treats as withhold. Right: it is the object door's rule, reached by the object door's function, with the object door's three D6 tiers (fault on a thrown or emptied own object, `private, no-store` on an undetermined own object, withhold on an unresolvable related object).

Accept-set changes, each judged:

1. `GET /meta/action` list, REST (`meta-collection-routes.ts` through `createMetaListAnswer`) and dispatcher (`answerMetaList`), step 7a. A withheld entry is left out; one owner whose posture throws or whose projection empties fails the whole page with the field-visibility fault, as the `object` list does (D5(2), "a hole no client can see"); the page carries `private, no-store` when any entry's posture was undetermined. The validator is computed over the served list (`metaRepresentationCaching`, `private, no-cache`), so cohorts never share a `304` across different bodies. Right.
2. `GET /meta/action/:name`, uncached arm (`createMetaItemAnswer` step 4a, both transports). A withheld entry is the chain's step-1 `absent` refusal, sent by the same code path as a name with nothing behind it (`sendMetaItemAbsent` on REST, `deps.error('Not found', 404)` on the dispatcher). Byte-identical by construction, not by comparison. Right.
3. `GET /meta/action/:name`, REST cached arm, the default door. `If-None-Match` is withheld from `getMetaItemCached` for `action` (`actionProjects`), so the protocol cannot answer `304` before the projection; I read `protocol-search-and-cache.ts` on `main` and it judges `ifNoneMatch` alone, never `If-Modified-Since`, so no second validator reaches a `304` first. After the projection: withheld answers `sendMetaItemAbsent`; fault answers the field-visibility fault; undetermined owner answers `private, no-store` with no `ETag`; served and determined compares the request validator to the protocol's, and that value equals the emitted `ETag` because every fingerprint the arm folds for an `action` is empty. A shared validator is correct here because a served entry is the same bytes for every caller it is served to; the only per-caller variation is served-or-absent, and absent carries no validator. The ordering is the ADR's `fetch, project, send`. Right.
4. `/layers` and `?layers=true`, both transports (`createMetaLayeredAnswer` step 3a). Every present layer is projected under one memoised source; an owner read off any layer stands in for a layer that names none; any layer withheld answers the whole read `absent` through step 1's refusal. Fail-closed is right: a layered view with one layer missing is a different shape from the plain answer and would say, by its shape, that the name exists. The `draft` layer is judged as an action entry like the others; it reaches only callers the stored-version door admits, who hold the write capability and are therefore D4-exempt in every shipped permission set, so no member depends on how a stored draft row is shaped. Right.
5. `/published`, REST (`registerMetaItemPublishedRoute`, after the gate and the object mask) and dispatcher (`servePublished`). A withheld entry answers the literal `404 { NOT_FOUND, Not found }` on REST and `deps.error('Not found', 404)` on the dispatcher; I read both doors' unknown-name tails and they are those same bodies. Right.
6. MCP `list_actions` (`servedActionObject`). The PR #31075 inline rule is replaced by a call to the seam over the same masker; an owner-less entry (`isObjectLessActionKey`) and an owner that names no served object are judged through the owner-less arm; a fault throws the door's own `fieldVisibilityRefusal`. Summaries receive a lookup so a param bound through `objectOverride` is described from the field of the object it names. The lookup hands back the raw target object, which is safe only because the seam has already judged that field readable for this caller before the summary runs; the own object handed to the summary is the projected one. `run_action`, `resume_run` and `capabilityRefusal` read the declarations unchanged. Right.
7. `summarizeAction`, `summarizeActionParams`, `resolveDeclaredActionParams` take an optional lookup; `enforceActionParams` passes none, pinned by a unit test that compares the two readings and the refusal sentence. The run doors (`POST /actions`, MCP `run_action`) are byte-identical. Right.
8. New exports (`projectMetaActionForCaller`, `projectMetaActionItem`, two types) on `@objectstack/rest`; two helpers on `@objectstack/metadata-core`. Additive, consumed by `@objectstack/runtime` in the same diff. Right.

Consumer hunt, on `main`, every reader of `/meta/action` (list or item), `/layers` and `/published`:

- Console. The only reader of `GET /meta/action` is Setup › Packaged automation (`PackagedActionsSection.tsx`, `packagedActions.ts`): an operator page reached under `setup.access`, which `OBJECT_SCHEMA_READ_ONLY_EXEMPT_CAPABILITIES` exempts, so it is answered as before; it also tolerates an empty answer by design. Record-page action buttons are rendered from `objectDef.actions`, the object schema served by `/meta/object` (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx`), which `main` already projects; no console path renders record or toolbar actions from `/meta/action`. App navigation items of `type: 'action'` carry a name and dispatch to the run door (`useNavActionDispatch.ts`); they read no action definition. The Studio and metadata-admin readers of `/layers` (`ResourceEditPage`, `EmbeddedItemEditor`, `LayeredDiff`, `ObjectActionsPanel`, `pairObjectActions`, `StudioNavItemInspector`) are authoring surfaces under `studio.access` or `manage_metadata`, both exempt.
- Client SDK. `@objectstack/client`'s `listActions` targets the automation descriptors route, not `/meta/action`; its generic `meta.get`, `meta.getCached`, `meta.layered` and `meta.getPublished` are pass-through readers with no action-specific contract. `@objectstack/client-react`'s metadata hooks read object schemas.
- CLI, examples, skills. No reader of `/meta/action`; the one skill eval that names the route names its write door. `content/docs` states nothing that the narrowing contradicts; the two pages that describe the projection are updated in this diff.
- A member who can run an action but can no longer read its entry. The run door still runs it, so nothing a member could do is taken away; what is taken away is the entry's statement that a field exists, which is D1's own promise. It is consistent with `/meta/object/X`, which already withholds the same action from that object's `actions` on `main`; before this diff the standalone entry contradicted the object door for the same caller.

No legitimate caller loses an answer it reads today. The accept set narrows for exactly one class: a non-exempt caller holding a `readable: false` field that a standalone or owner-less action binds, on a deployment with a `security` service and the mask on.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/runtime` is the level the Post-Task Checklist step 3 gives a non-protocol narrowing: `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (no key, accepted value or type an author writes moves; the two new exports and the optional lookup parameter are additive), and `none` takes `patch`. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is BREAKING by that same rule, so the `!` in the title and the changeset's first line, the BREAKING banner, and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker (a category the gate lists) are all consistent with each other; nothing authorable is removed, so no migration and no tombstone are owed. Both declaration lines appear line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body.

`Skills-docs:` is present, as a `(narrowing)` arm requires, and its substance is true: `skills/**` teaches no `/meta` action read and the two docs pages are updated in the diff. Its spelling, `no move — …`, is outside the closed set the dispatch template fixes (`updated here | follow-up owed — FILES | follow-up #N | none — REASON`). No gate reads the line, so this is a should-fix on the PR body and changeset, not a block: `updated here` is the truthful spelling for a diff that teaches the rule in the docs.

### ③ Boundary flags

Judged at rule level; mechanisms stay out of this record.

- (a) The run doors resolve an `objectOverride` param's type and options on the own object. This is a param-validation question under ADR-0104 D2, not a disclosure one; changing it changes refusal text and the accepted value set at the run door, which is its own changeset and its own card. Separate step. Not a block.
- (b) The `/meta` doors read an entry's owner from `objectName` only; an entry carrying only the legacy `object` key is judged owner-less there, while `collectActionDeclarations` (and so MCP) still honours that key as the owner. The two doors can therefore disagree about one entry, and on the `/meta` doors such an entry's own-object `field` params are not judged at all: that is serving on a guess, which the fail-closed rule the PR itself states for an undetermined target does not allow. The same holds for an owner that names no object definition in the list read: with no `objectOverride` params the entry is served as declared. Should-fix: either read the legacy owner key as the declarations collector does and withhold an entry binding own-object fields whose owner cannot be resolved, or state the `objectName`-only reading in the changeset so the shipped CHANGELOG does not claim more than the doors do. Not a block: on every path `main` served the entry whole, so the head is strictly narrower than `main` and the remaining gap is coverage, not regression.
- (c) `GET /meta/action/:name/references` answers `200` for a withheld entry, naming objects only. It serves no field, label or option, so nothing D1 protects reaches the caller through it, but it does say by its status that the name exists. Should-fix in a separate step: that door's absence answer should follow the item read's, as `/published` and `/layers` now do.
- (d) App navigation items name actions. A name in a navigation item is served by the app door under the app's own gates and carries no field; the run it triggers is unchanged. Separate step, if any; nothing here is owed by this PR.
- (e) Inline actions embedded in views and pages are not run through this projection. Those documents are served by the `view` and `page` doors, which are not object-schema doors, and D1's "any plane" reaches them. Separate step with its own card; it is outside the narrowing this PR declares and does not weaken it.

### ④ Design judgment

One seam over `projectMetaObjectSchema` is the right shape: a second rule for standalone entries would have to be proven equal to the object door's on every position `object-schema-fls-references.ts` enumerates, and would drift; building the object document and asking the object door's own function makes equality structural. The cost is honest: for a `project` posture the item doors now read the object list to find the owner. Probes against the cited code on `main`:

- Owner-less (global) actions. No own object, so only `objectOverride` params can bind a field; each target is asked through the transport's masker and related as readable-set or `undefined`. A target whose posture throws or is undetermined withholds the entry, which is the object door's rule for a related object (unlike its own-object tiers, and deliberately so: nothing of another object is served on a guess). An entry with no target is served as declared. Holds.
- An `objectOverride` naming an object that does not exist. Owned arm: `relate` asks the security service, gets no array, relates `undefined`, withholds. Owner-less arm: the masker throws or answers undetermined, the target is related `undefined`, withholds. Holds, fail-closed on both arms.
- An action with no params. Nothing binds a field, so the only positions judged are the entry's other field-reading positions, as on the object door. Served as declared. Holds.
- Flow-backed params. The projection judges declared params; a flow's screen fields are not object fields and the object door has never judged them. `summarizeActionParams` keeps its flow reading. Consistent with the object door; not widened by this diff.
- A caller with no readable field on an owner. The own-object projection empties, which is the D6 fault, and on the list door it fails the whole page. This is exactly what `GET /meta/object` already does for that caller, so the action list is no worse than the object list for them; a deployment living in that state is already loud there.
- Cache keys shared across callers. The protocol cache keeps one document per type, name, locale and environment with no caller dimension, and every projection here runs after that cache, per D3. The list door's validator is over the served list; the cached item arm's validator is the protocol's, which is correct because a served entry is caller-invariant and a withheld one carries no validator. No shared store can hand a projected caller another cohort's body.
- The cached arm's validator reuse. A validator issued to an unrestricted caller and presented by a restricted one is answered the absence body, never `304`; a restricted caller whose permission is later granted is answered `304` on a match, which is right because the body is identical. `If-Modified-Since` cannot shortcut this: the protocol never judges it.
- Two observations, neither a block. First, `metaActionProjectionSources` resolves an owner by listing every object through `listMetaItems('object')` even for a single item read, although `MetaReadGateListSource.getObjectItem` is a by-name read on the same source; a cost, not a contract matter. Second, a protocol with an item read but no list read makes the item door throw a `TypeError` for a `project` posture rather than answer the field-visibility fault; no shipped protocol has that shape, and loud is the right default for it.

On the narrowing face the question is whether the narrowing takes a declared capability away at the consumer or makes the spec's own refusal real. It makes D1 real on the action doors for `objectName`-owned and owner-less entries, and takes nothing a consumer reads today away; the one declared-owner spelling it does not yet read is named in ③(b).

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · 2026-11-07T09:18Z · head `c97eb416db5710fcd97a0193aa5f2f7433248331`

- **Contract review:** PASS at this head, at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the narrowing face, record 6704723718. It was conditional on CI, and every check-run is now green. There is no must-fix. Its should-fixes go into this seat's follow-up list, and none of them changes what lands here:
  - the `Skills-docs:` line respelled into the template's closed set;
  - the owner read also taking the legacy `object` key, or withholding an entry whose owner names no object definition;
  - the action references door answering a withheld entry the way the item read does.
- **What lands:** each `/meta` action read projects a standalone action entry through the object door's own ADR-0106 projection. That covers the list, the item read (cached and uncached), `/layers` with `?layers=true`, and `/published`, on REST and on the runtime dispatcher.
